GENERAL.HOUSING_OCCUPANTS_TOOLTIP:
Villagers occupy houses closer to their Workplaces and Needs. The houses must have free space and be of expected Quality. 

Occupants of higher Status expect houses of higher Quality. They will upgrade their houses if they meet all Desirability requirements. Otherwise, they will move out.
GENERAL.HOUSING_QUALITY_INFO_TOOLTIP:
Housing Quality is determined by the surrounding Desirability and demands from the correct status. 

To upgrade a house, make sure all Desirability requirements are met and that Villagers of the correct status demand Housing. 

On the other hand, houses will eventually return to their previous Quality if the requirements are no longer met.
GENERAL.HOUSING_QUALITY_1_TOOLTIP: Low-Quality houses are built by default within painted Residential areas. They are suitable for Serfs only.
GENERAL.HOUSING_QUALITY_2_TOOLTIP: Medium-Quality houses require a Beautification area away from Undesirable areas. They are suitable for Commoners.
GENERAL.HOUSING_BEAUTIFICATION_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be within a Beautification area. Make sure to place Decorations or Buildings that provide Beautification to fulfil this condition.
GENERAL.HOUSING_SPLENDOR_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be within a Splendour area. Make sure to place Decorations or Buildings that provide Splendour to fulfil this condition. Splendour can come from any Estate.
GENERAL.HOUSING_NEIGHBORHOOD_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be built in desirable neighbourhoods, away from noisy or dirty environments. Such places have a negative Desirability area.
GENERAL.HOUSING_COMMONER_TOOLTIP: Commoners need to be looking for Medium-Quality Housing.
GENERAL.HOUSING_NOPREQUISITE_TOOLTIP: Houses with no requirements can be built anywhere.
GENERAL.HOUSING_ZONING_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be within a painted Residential Area. Make sure to keep the Residential Area painted to fulfil this condition.
GENERAL.NEEDS_ESSENTIAL_TOOLTIP:
Essential Needs affect the Villager's Happiness, which you should always aim to fulfil. 

When these Needs go unmet, Happiness drops, which may compel the Villager to leave.
GENERAL.NEEDS_ADDITIONAL_TOOLTIP:
Like Essential Needs, Additional Needs affect the Villager's Happiness. 

These can be fulfilled at your own pace, as they only become necessary when promoting a villager to a new status or if you want to raise your villager's Happiness. 

After being filled once, Happiness penalties apply when left in decline, which might compel villagers to leave.
GENERAL.NEEDS_GUEST_TOOLTIP:
Guest Needs affect the Guest's Happiness, which you should always aim to fulfil. 

When these Needs go unmet, Happiness drops, which may dampen the Guest's appreciation of your village.
GENERAL.FAVORITE_DESC: Favouriting a resource places it in the upper section of the Resources panel near the top of the screen, while non-favourite resources will be displayed in the lower section.
GENERAL.HOUSING_LIGHT_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be within a Light Fortification area. Make sure to place buildings nearby that provide Light or Heavy Fortification to fulfil this condition.
GENERAL.HOUSING_HEAVY_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be within a Heavy Fortification area. Make sure to place buildings nearby that provide Heavy Fortification nearby to fulfil this condition.
GENERAL.HOUSING_PATROL_TOOLTIP: Houses need to be protected by patrols. Make sure to paint a patrolling area over the houses and have enough patrollers to secure all painted buildings.
GENERAL.HOUSING_DENSITY_INFO_TOOLTIP:
Housing Density is determined by surrounding Fortifications and Patrols.

To upgrade a house, make sure they are located within suitable Fortification areas and covered by sufficient Patrols. 

On the other hand, houses will eventually return to their previous Density if the Fortification or Patrol coverage is not met.
GENERAL.HOUSING_DENSITY_1_TOOLTIP: Low-Density houses are built by default within painted Residential areas. They can hold a small number of villagers.
GENERAL.HOUSING_DENSITY_2_TOOLTIP: Medium-Density houses require Light Fortification and sufficient patrol coverage. They can hold a fair number of villagers.
GENERAL.CONDITION_LIGHT_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP: This building needs to be constructed within a Light Fortification area. Make sure to place buildings nearby that provide Light or Heavy Fortification to fulfil this condition.
GENERAL.CONDITION_HEAVY_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP: This building needs to be constructed within a Heavy Fortification area. Make sure to place buildings nearby that provide Heavy Fortification to fulfil this condition.

ESTATES.SPLENDOR_WITH_ESTATE_X_GAIN_DESC:
{1} Splendour is earned from the most impressive buildings of the {1} Estate.

{1} Splendour plays a key role in calculating your Influence Cap with the {1} Estate and also contributes to your overall Prosperity.

{1} Splendour has no value limits.
ESTATES.INFLUENCE_WITH_ESTATE_X_DESC:
{1} Influence is favour earned through mandates, missions, and quests with the {1} Estate.

 It can be spent to unlock new progression content with the {1} Estate and access new options during events. 

Will gradually shift towards the Influence Cap.

{1} Influence ranges from -100 to 100.
ESTATES.X_ESTATE_RATING_DESC:
Rating is the perception an Estate has of your village.

{1} Rating is required to unlock new progression content and also determines the {1} Estate Influence Cap. This value is affected by both your Splendour with {1} and how exclusively you are invested toward it.

{1} Rating has no value limits.
ESTATES.INFLUENCE_CAP_WITH_ESTATE_X_DESC:
Influence gained beyond the Cap will naturally decrease down to this value. Splendour increases the Influence Cap of its estate.

Influence Cap ranges from -50 to 50.
